title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: Pollard-rho distinguished-point inversion in GT

claims.statement: For each production instance with nonidentity P in G1 and z in GT (including z=1), compute g=e(P,Q0)=pairing(Q0,P,final_exponentiate=True), solve a=log_g z by a distinguished-point Pollard-rho walk in the prime-order group GT, and return Q=[a]Q0. The Las Vegas algorithm succeeds with probability 1 over uniform P, z and fresh coins, retrying the negligible degenerate or aborted walk events. Its expected total computation is at most 2^127.798437 target-group-operation equivalents (C=20,000 instructions per dense Fp12 multiplication), including preprocessing, all walks and restarts, detection delay, hashing and lookup, verification, scalar multiplication and output. Peak memory is at most 2^57.484435 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^22 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in the total; nonuniform advice is 0. No auxiliary powers are used. The score is log2(W)=127.798437. This is a generic attack bound, not a claim of novelty or practical execution; the disclosed heuristic is the standard random-mapping model for the walk.

experiments.purpose: Run the exact exponent bookkeeping, distinguished-endpoint walks and collision equation in an additive group of prime order. This validates the algebra and the retry path for degenerate collisions at toy scope; it does not establish production curve behavior, Fp12 costs, memory bounds or the random-mapping constant.
